source_testimonies.utilitarian:
Action–Consequence Table (all probabilities = 1 unless noted)

1. Pull the lever  
• One worker: death; harm; magnitude = very high; permanent; irreversible; STATED  
• Five workers: survive; benefit; magnitude = very high; lifelong; irreversible; STATED  
• Work site: warning signal stops; minor benefit (clarity, calm); low magnitude; reversible; STATED

2. Do not pull the lever  
• One worker: survives; benefit; very high; lifelong; irreversible; STATED  
• Five workers: death; harm; very high; permanent; irreversible; STATED  
• Work site: warning signal continues; minor harm (noise, confusion); low magnitude; reversible; STATED

Impact ranking  
Very-high, certain deaths/survivals dwarf the low-magnitude signal effects. Saving four additional lives (5-1) under “pull” dominates.

Missing information that could reverse judgment  
• If the single worker’s life expectancy or social impact exceeded that of the five combined by >4×.  
• If pulling the lever imposed large hidden harms (legal chaos, future deterrence) outweighing four lives. These are UNKNOWN.

Comparison  
Pull lever: net +4 lives.  
Do nothing: net –4 lives relative to the alternative.

Utilitarian assessment  
Given equal moral weight per life and no stated offsetting factors, the aggregate well-being is maximized by pulling the lever.

Utilitarian Status: PULL LEVER, unless the unknown, unstated factors above make the lone worker’s loss greater than the combined loss of five, which the scenario does not indicate.
source_testimonies.deontological:
Action: PULL_LEVER  
1. Maxim: “Whenever I can save several by intentionally redirecting a lethal threat onto one, I will do so.” Universal-law test: A rational agent could not will universal readiness to kill an innocent as a mere means; the single victim’s agency would be overridden. Maxim fails.  
2. Satisfies: imperfect duty of rescue (save five).  
   Violates: perfect duties of non-instrumentalization and autonomy, right not to be killed, duty of justice (equal juridical standing).  
3. Classification: PROHIBITED (perfect duties outweigh).  
4. Conflict: rescue vs non-killing. Priority rule: Perfect duties to respect humanity as an end override imperfect duties of beneficence.  
5. Numerical magnitude: IRRELEVANT (cannot trade one person’s inviolable right for aggregate lives).  

Action: REFRAIN  
1. Maxim: “When saving several would require me to kill an innocent, I will refrain from killing.” Universal-law test: All can will this; it preserves each person’s status as end-in-themselves.  
2. Satisfies: non-instrumentalization, autonomy, justice, right not to be killed.  
   Violates: imperfect duty of rescue toward the five.  
3. Classification: REQUIRED (acts in accordance with undefeated perfect duties).  
4. Conflict: same as above; resolved by perfect-over-imperfect hierarchy.  
5. Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY (establishes the scope of rescue duty but cannot override the prohibition on killing).
source_testimonies.virtue:
Action label: “PULL THE LEVER”  
• Actor’s role: a witness suddenly responsible for the rail switch—quasi-guardian of all workers present.  
• Virtues it expresses: compassion (saving five), responsibility, resolute courage to act under terror.  
• Vices it risks: presumptuous hubris (authoring a death), callousness toward the single victim, possible rashness if facts uncertain.  
• Circumstances phronesis must notice: Maria’s unique power to intervene, certainty of outcomes, absence of time for deeper consultation, the stopped warning signal (future safety?).  
• Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY—saving more lives supports compassion, yet sheer count never by itself justifies killing.  

Action label: “DO NOT PULL THE LEVER”  
• Actor’s role: passive observer retaining moral innocence but neglecting protective duty.  
• Virtues it expresses: humility about taking life, respect for the worker’s inviolability.  
• Vices it risks: cowardice, culpable indifference, failure of beneficence toward the five.  
• Circumstances: same certainty of death, but no direct bodily interference.  
• Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY—non-intervention keeps hands “clean” but lets larger harm occur.

Central virtue conflict: nonmaleficent respect for each individual life vs compassionate responsibility to reduce avoidable tragedy.

Practical-wisdom comparison rule: when the agent already stands in a protector role and can foreseeably prevent grave harm without vicious motive, courageous beneficence may justifiably override the presumption against direct harm.

Provisional judgment: PULL THE LEVER better aligns with an integrated character of courageous, compassionate guardianship—yet the conflict makes final assessment humbling. Virtue-Ethics Status: NORMATIVELY_CONTESTED.
source_testimonies.care:
Care–ethical comparison of Maria’s two options

1. Relational mapping for each option  
   a. If Maria pulls the lever  
      • Direct entrustment: Maria intervenes and thereby places one particular worker in a position of fatal vulnerability that she herself created.  
      • Dependency: The five workers on the main track become dependent on Maria’s willingness to act; the single worker on the side track becomes dependent on her restraint.  
      • Trust: No prior personal trust is described. All six workers are equally unknown to Maria.  
      • Responsibility generated by action: By pulling, Maria actively authors the side-track worker’s peril.  
      • Responsiveness to need: Pulling responds to the immediate life-or-death need of the five who will otherwise be killed.  
      • Agent-created vulnerability: Yes, toward the one worker.  
      • Numerical magnitude: Five lives spared versus one life lost. Because the relational factors are symmetrical except for agent-created vulnerability, the head-count becomes the tie-breaker.

   b. If Maria does not pull the lever  
      • Direct entrustment: Maria refrains from intervening; the fatal situation of the five workers was not authored by her.  
      • Dependency: The five workers remain fatally dependent on an inoperative warning system, not on Maria.  
      • Trust: Again, no special tie.  
      • Responsibility generated by inaction: Maria allows an existing danger to proceed unaltered.  
      • Responsiveness to need: She ignores an urgent and addressable need of five workers.  
      • Agent-created vulnerability: None additional; the original danger persists.  
      • Numerical magnitude: One life spared, five lost.

2. Testing the relational factors head-to-head  
   • Origin of vulnerability: Pulling lever creates new vulnerability for one person; not pulling perpetuates existing vulnerability for five. Care ethics gives moral weight to not generating new harm, but it equally stresses being responsive to actual, concrete suffering when one is in a privileged position to help.  
   • Depth of dependency: In the instant Maria notices the scenario, both groups become dependents in her moral field; neither has an antecedent stronger claim.  
   • Quality of responsiveness: Pulling lever embodies attentive and competent care toward the larger group in danger; inaction withholds that care.

3. Role of numerical magnitude  
   Designation: DECISIVE. Because the relational profile (no pre-existing relationships, symmetrical entrustment once Maria becomes aware) is otherwise even, the only remaining difference is how many human beings receive the life-preserving care that Maria can provide.

4. Care-Ethics Status  
   NORMATIVELY_CONTESTED but leaning toward action. Some care theorists place great weight on “first, do no new harm,” which would support non-intervention. Others emphasize active responsiveness to concrete need, which favors intervention. Given the relational symmetry, the pull option better embodies attentive responsiveness to the greatest number of equally placed dependents.

Provisional recommendation  
Maria should pull the lever. While she sadly imposes a fatal vulnerability on one worker, she offers life-saving care to five others whose situation is otherwise hopeless, and no prior relationship singles out the lone worker for preferential protection. The warning signal’s cessation slightly reduces general chaos but is morally secondary here. Maria should also remain emotionally present to the tragedy she has helped shape, acknowledging responsibility and seeking restorative engagement with all affected parties thereafter.
[/INST]

source_testimonies.rawlsian:
Actions compared: PULL_LEVER vs REFRAIN

Least-advantaged group under each action  
• PULL_LEVER: the single diverged-track worker who is killed (loses life—a basic liberty).  
• REFRAIN: the five main-track workers who are killed (lose the same basic liberty).

Basic-liberty comparison  
Life/security is a basic liberty that must be protected equally. Both actions leave at least one person dead, so neither secures that liberty completely. Because the liberty lost is identical, we next examine how fairly the risk of that loss is distributed behind the veil of ignorance.

Fair-equality-of-opportunity / risk distribution  
Behind the veil, an agent does not know whether she will be any one of the six workers. PULL_LEVER assigns each person a 1-in-6 risk of death; REFRAIN imposes a 5-in-6 risk. A rational chooser subject to maximin reasoning prefers the action that minimises one’s chance of falling into the worst position while keeping basic liberties otherwise constant.

Numerical magnitude status  
DECISIVE only as a risk-distribution fact affecting each individual’s security of the same basic liberty, not as an aggregate welfare tally.

Rawlsian conclusion  
PULL_LEVER better protects each person’s fair security of the basic liberty of life than REFRAIN.  
Rawlsian Status: ACTION_PREFERRED = PULL_LEVER
[/INST]

last_response.answer: The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods. No basic liberty (e.g., political freedom, speech, integrity) is differentially restricted by either action; each scenario involves an identical external accident. Therefore the lexical first principle is not triggered and we proceed to the second principle. Because life and bodily security are prerequisite primary goods for pursuing any plan, we treat survival as part of the basic-interest security subset of primary goods. Under veil-of-ignorance uncertainty, a rational representative would choose the action that maximises the minimum prospect of retaining that good. Pulling the lever reduces the worst-off position from "certain death for five" to "certain death for one," so maximin favours A0. last_response.answer: The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods. No basic liberty (e.g., political freedom, speech, integrity) is differentially restricted by either action; each scenario involves an identical external accident. Therefore the lexical first principle is not triggered and we proceed to the second principle. Because life and bodily security are prerequisite primary goods for pursuing any plan, we treat survival as part of the basic-interest security subset of primary goods. Under veil-of-ignorance uncertainty, a rational representative would choose the action that maximises the minimum prospect of retaining that good. Pulling the lever reduces the worst-off position from "certain death for five" to "certain death for one," so maximin favours A0. challenge_response.answer: The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods. No basic liberty (e.g., political freedom, speech, integrity) is differentially restricted by either action; each scenario involves an identical external accident. Therefore the lexical first principle is not triggered and we proceed to the second principle. Because life and bodily security are prerequisite primary goods for pursuing any plan, we treat survival as part of the basic-interest security subset of primary goods. Under veil-of-ignorance uncertainty, a rational representative would choose the action that maximises the minimum prospect of retaining that good. Pulling the lever reduces the worst-off position from "certain death for five" to "certain death for one," so maximin favours A0. last_response.answer: The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods. No basic liberty (e.g., political freedom, speech, integrity) is differentially restricted by either action; each scenario involves an identical external accident. Therefore the lexical first principle is not triggered and we proceed to the second principle. Because life and bodily security are prerequisite primary goods for pursuing any plan, we treat survival as part of the basic-interest security subset of primary goods. Under veil-of-ignorance uncertainty, a rational representative would choose the action that maximises the minimum prospect of retaining that good. Pulling the lever reduces the worst-off position from "certain death for five" to "certain death for one," so maximin favours A0.
